Stuttgart — It depends on exactly where: the whole city rule only bans diesel Euro‑4 or older (so Euro‑5 can enter), but the smaller central “environmental zone” covering the Stuttgart basin and parts of Bad Cannstatt, Feuerbach and Zuffenhausen currently bans Euro‑5 and older. agent.text:
Short answer — you risk being treated as having no vignette and owing the substitute toll (€200 for cars). A quick checklist:

- What decides a fine: (1) a digital vignette only counts for the exact licence plate and country you entered; (2) typos can be corrected free only before the vignette’s validity starts; (3) after start, 1‑day / 10‑day / 2‑month vignettes cannot be changed — only annual vignettes can (for €18). Source: ASFINAG tolling rules and licence‑plate info.  
  [ASFINAG Tolling Regulations v87 (ENG)](https://media.asfinag.at/media/00sbusiu/00_mo_v87_tolling-regulations_en.pdf) · [ASFINAG toll shop — licence plate changes](https://shop.asfinag.at/en/info-pages/license-plate/)

What to do now (immediately):
1. Buy a new digital vignette right away with the correct plate (ASFINAG shop or app) so you have legal cover for the correct plate for your travel day. [ASFINAG shop](https://shop.asfinag.at/en)  
2. Keep the purchase confirmation (screenshot/email) as proof.  
3. If you cannot buy a correct vignette before you drive, expect the substitute toll (Ersatzmaut) of €200 for a car; if unpaid, higher administrative fines may follow (see the tolling regulation).  

If your original was an annual vignette, contact ASFINAG to request the plate change (€18).

baseline.text: Unfortunately, once a 10‑day digital vignette’s validity has started you cannot correct the plate. The vignette only counts for the exact plate/country entered, so the typo means it’s not valid for your actual plate. Annual vignettes can be changed for €18, but 1‑day, 10‑day and 2‑month vignettes cannot. Buy a new 10‑day vignette with the correct plate to be legal (or switch to an annual if that suits you).
